title: Viva Glint: choose whether to retain or erase survey data for deleted users
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, admin controls, retention behaviour and licensing statements are supported. Microsoft Learn still carries the Entra processing pause alongside its stated restart date, and the briefing accurately preserves that uncertainty.

claims.claim: Viva Glint has a User Data control named Retain survey responses and identifiable data for deleted users.
claims.quote:
## User Data
Configure how Glint data and user data is handled for your Microsoft Viva Glint instance.
### Retain survey responses and identifiable data for deleted users

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no API or automation call for the deleted-user retention switch as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Viva Glint retain survey responses identifiable data deleted users API Microsoft Graph PowerShell retention policy delete user; site:learn.microsoft.com/graph Viva Glint delete user retention settings API; Viva Glint retention PowerShell. Opened General Settings, deletion and FAQ pages.

claims.claim: Manual user deletion is at Viva Glint admin dashboard > Configuration > Employees > People > user > Actions > Delete User.
claims.quote:
From the admin dashboard, select the Configuration symbol, then in Employees choose People.
Search for the user in the Search People field.
On the user's profile, select Delete User from the Actions dropdown menu.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no API or automation equivalent for deleting a Viva Glint user.
claims.quote: Searched: Viva Glint API delete users; site:learn.microsoft.com/graph Viva Glint delete user retention settings API. Opened Responding to DSRs, Delete user data and FAQ pages; results document dashboard deletion, not a Glint delete-user endpoint.

claims.claim: Data retention policy is at Viva Glint admin dashboard > Configuration > Service Configuration > General Settings > User Data > Data retention policy.
claims.quote:
Select the Configuration symbol on your Viva Glint admin dashboard and then General Settings in the Service Configuration section.
## User Data
### Data retention policy
Use the Data retention policy control to define the data retention policy for your Glint instance.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no API or automation call for the Glint Data retention policy setting as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Viva Glint Data retention policy API configure months user deletion REST API; Viva Glint retention PowerShell. Opened General Settings; read data residency and Purview retention-cmdlet search excerpts, which do not document an operation for this Glint setting.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; controls[0].note; rationales
claims.claim: Off erases all data related to the requester, including survey responses and associated identifiers and reporting data.
claims.quote: If this setting is Off, it deletes the user's survey responses, first name, last name, employee ID, email address and personal email (if used) associated with those survey responses and reporting.

claims.claim: The deleted-user retention configuration is platform-wide and applies equally to all delete requests.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Why it matters; Scope; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: One General Settings value applies to all survey programs in the selected Viva Glint instance.
claims.quote:
Any initial actions or subsequent changes in General Settings apply to all survey programs in your Viva Glint platform.
Configure how Glint data and user data is handled for your Microsoft Viva Glint instance.

claims.where: What's changing; controls[1].note; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: A deleted user's employee record remains soft-deleted for 30 days rather than being immediately permanently deleted.
claims.quote: When Viva Glint receives the delete signal from a Data Subject Request (DSR) or Microsoft Entra ID for a user, they're not immediately deleted. A user's employee record is in a soft-deleted state for 30 days.

claims.claim: During the soft-delete period, the existing employee record can be updated to the status in the HRIS file, subject to the employee-ID reuse control.
claims.quote: the employee record may be modified from its soft-deleted state and updated to the status provided in the Human Resource Information System (HRIS) file per the client's User Data control setting at Disregard Employee IDs of previously deleted employees.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: After the 30-day soft-delete period, permanent deletion proceeds in accordance with the User Data control.
claims.quote: After the 30-day period, all data related to the employee is permanently deleted in accordance with User Data controls.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Permanently deleted survey responses and identifiable data cannot be restored.
claims.quote: Permanently deleted survey responses and identifiable data can't be restored.

claims.claim: Disregard Employee IDs of previously deleted employees set to Off updates soft-deleted records when uploaded employee IDs and email addresses match.
claims.quote: Off | Update the already soft deleted records with the status provided in the HRIS file. Note: The uploaded employee IDs and email addresses must match the soft deleted user records.

claims.claim: Disregard Employee IDs of previously deleted employees defaults to On, excluding associated data from uploads.
claims.quote: On (default) | Exclude data associated with employee IDs of previously removed employees from uploads.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: As read in November 2026, Learn still says Microsoft Entra delete-signal processing is paused until September 30, 2026.
claims.quote: Processing of delete signals from Microsoft Entra in Viva Glint is paused until September 30, 2026.

claims.claim: The FAQ says live Microsoft Entra delete-signal processing starts again on October 1, 2026.
claims.quote: Starting October 1, 2026, we will start processing these live signals once again.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: The historical Microsoft Entra delete signals described in the FAQ cover June 2025 to September 2026.
claims.quote: We will also be processing the historical delete signals received from Microsoft Entra for the period June 2025 - September 2026 following the same user data control settings.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Historical and live Microsoft Entra delete signals are processed in alignment with the deleted-user retention setting.
claims.quote: All data related to the employee is permanently deleted in alignment with the client's User Data control settings at Retain survey responses and identifiable data for deleted users.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: From September 1, 2026, the FAQ offers only retain or erase, not de-identification while retaining survey responses.
claims.quote: No, starting September 1, 2026 we only offer the ability for customers to either retain all survey responses and identifiable data for deleted users

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: A previous Delete survey data for deleted users value of Off is carried over as On for the new retention control.
claims.quote: If you previously had Delete survey data for deleted users set to Off, we will toggle this new control Retain survey responses and identifiable data for deleted users to On and vice-versa.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: A previous Delete survey data for deleted users value of On is carried over as Off for the new retention control.
claims.quote: If you previously had Delete survey data for deleted users set to Off, we will toggle this new control Retain survey responses and identifiable data for deleted users to On and vice-versa.

claims.claim: Historical processing does not delete user records when detected hierarchy changes caused user statuses to change.
claims.quote: During historical signal processing, user records will not be deleted if hierarchy changes were detected that caused user statuses to be modified.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft advises reviewing Active and Inactive user lists for people who should have Deleted status but have not been deleted.
claims.quote: Review the list of active and inactive users to identify any users who should have a Deleted status but have not yet been deleted.

claims.claim: Deleted Glint users are removed from distribution lists.
claims.quote: When a user is deleted from Glint, they are removed from distribution lists and future surveys.

claims.claim: Deleted Glint users are removed from future surveys.
claims.quote: When a user is deleted from Glint, they are removed from distribution lists and future surveys.

claims.claim: A deleted user's role definitions are removed.
claims.quote: The user's role definitions and their reporting permissions are removed.

claims.claim: A deleted user's reporting permissions are removed.
claims.quote: The user's role definitions and their reporting permissions are removed.

claims.claim: A deleted user's direct reports are assigned to a placeholder name.
claims.quote: If the user has direct reports, their reports are assigned to a placeholder name, which can be updated later.

claims.claim: The placeholder name assigned to direct reports can be updated later.
claims.quote: If the user has direct reports, their reports are assigned to a placeholder name, which can be updated later.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft says not to create a new user record reusing a deleted user's email address or employee ID during the 30-day soft-delete period.
claims.quote: When a user is deleted, their employee record remains in a soft-deleted state for 30 days. During this period, don't create a new user record with the same email address or employee ID.

claims.claim: Reusing identifiers during the soft-delete period can cause upload failures.
claims.quote: Don't create a new user record or reuse the same identifiers for another user during the 30-day soft-delete period. Reusing identifiers too soon can cause sign-in, sync, or upload conflicts.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The control is an included option inside Viva Glint, whose use requires a Viva Suite or Viva Glint subscription plan.
claims.quote: The purchase of a Viva Suite or Viva Glint subscription plan is required for using Microsoft Viva Glint.

claims.claim: Active subscription licences must cover at least the number of active users in the app.

claims.claim: Individual user licence assignment is not required for using Viva Glint.

Each Viva Glint experience allows Viva Glint Admins to independently manage:

claims.where: Scope; Governance guidance: At rollout; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Viva Glint Admins, as data controllers, can choose the retain or erase value.
claims.quote: Viva Glint Admins, as data controllers, can choose to either: retain all survey responses and identifiable data for deleted users

claims.claim: Data retention policy is a separate control governing how long Glint holds survey data, rather than the deleted-user retain-or-erase decision.
claims.quote:
### Data retention policy
Define how long you would like Viva Glint to hold onto your Glint survey data for.

claims.claim: Data retention policy defaults to Until subscription ends, retaining data indefinitely while the tenant has an active Glint subscription.
claims.quote: Until subscription ends (default) | Glint data is retained indefinitely as long as the tenant has an active Viva Glint subscription.

claims.claim: The minimum custom data retention period is 6 months.
claims.quote: Enter a numerical retention period (in months) to define the data retention time period. The value must be between 6-1000 months.

claims.claim: The maximum custom data retention period is 1000 months.
claims.quote: Enter a numerical retention period (in months) to define the data retention time period. The value must be between 6-1000 months.

claims.claim: Data retention policy applies to all Glint survey data.
claims.quote: This will apply to all Glint survey data including programs, 360 data, associated reporting conversations, actions, and more. This does not apply to configurations set in place.

claims.claim: No per-program or per-user value for the deleted-user retention setting is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Viva Glint roles permissions General Settings User Data retain deleted users per survey program; Viva Glint per-program Retain survey responses. Opened General Settings, Delete user data and FAQ; they document a platform-level value applying to all requests.

claims.claim: The feature pages name Viva Glint Admins as data controllers but do not specify additional roles or a setting-specific permissions matrix.
claims.quote: Searched: Viva Glint role definitions General Settings permissions. Opened General Settings, Delete user data, FAQ and Key roles for Viva Glint; read User Roles excerpts. None specifies additional roles or a permissions matrix for this retention switch.
